part.text: The file covers the full requested interval, January 1, 2013 through December 31, 2025. I’m comparing total crash counts, each weekday’s share of all crashes, and crashes per calendar occurrence of each weekday.

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: _make_weekday_outputs.py
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+weekdays = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
+
+data = duckdb.query(
+    """
+    SELECT dayofweek(crash_date) AS weekday_num, count(*) AS crash_count
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY weekday_num
+    ORDER BY weekday_num
+    """
+).df()
+# DuckDB dayofweek: Sunday=0; reorder as Monday through Sunday.
+data["weekday"] = data["weekday_num"].map(lambda n: weekdays[(int(n) - 1) % 7])
+data = data.set_index("weekday").reindex(weekdays).reset_index()
+data["crash_count"] = data["crash_count"].astype("int64")
+total = int(data["crash_count"].sum())
+data["share_pct"] = data["crash_count"] / total * 100
+
+dates = pd.date_range("2013-01-01", "2025-12-31", freq="D")
+occurrences = pd.Series(dates.day_name()).value_counts().reindex(weekdays)
+data["calendar_days"] = data["weekday"].map(occurrences).astype("int64")
+data["avg_crashes_per_day"] = data["crash_count"] / data["calendar_days"]
+
+# Option 1: total counts across the complete 13-year period.
+v1 = data[["weekday", "crash_count"]]
+v1.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.2))
+bars = ax.bar(data["weekday"], data["crash_count"], color="#3267a8")
+ax.bar_label(bars, labels=[f"{v:,.0f}" for v in data["crash_count"]], padding=3, fontsize=9)
+ax.set_title("NYC police-reported crashes by weekday, 2013–2025")
+ax.set_ylabel("Crashes")
+ax.set_xlabel("Day of week")
+ax.set_ylim(0, data["crash_count"].max() * 1.12)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=20)
+ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 2: each weekday's share of all crashes; pie chart emphasizes composition.
+v2 = data[["weekday", "crash_count", "share_pct"]]
+v2.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6.5))
+wedges, _, _ = ax.pie(
+    data["crash_count"],
+    startangle=90,
+    counterclock=False,
+    autopct=lambda pct: f"{pct:.1f}%",
+    pctdistance=0.75,
+    textprops={"fontsize": 9},
+    wedgeprops={"edgecolor": "white", "linewidth": 1},
+)
+ax.legend(
+    wedges,
+    [f"{d}: {n:,}" for d, n in zip(data["weekday"], data["crash_count"])],
+    title="Weekday (crash count)",
+    loc="center left",
+    bbox_to_anchor=(0.98, 0.5),
+    frameon=False,
+)
+ax.set_title("Share of all NYC police-reported crashes by weekday, 2013–2025")
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=160, bbox_inches="tight")
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Option 3: average count per calendar date of that weekday, normalizing for occurrences.
+v3 = data[["weekday", "crash_count", "calendar_days", "avg_crashes_per_day"]]
+v3.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5.2))
+ax.plot(data["weekday"], data["avg_crashes_per_day"], marker="o", linewidth=2, color="#c45135")
+for x, y in zip(data["weekday"], data["avg_crashes_per_day"]):
+    ax.annotate(f"{y:.1f}", (x, y), xytext=(0, 8), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=9)
+ax.set_title("Average NYC crashes per calendar day by weekday, 2013–2025")
+ax.set_ylabel("Crashes per occurrence of weekday")
+ax.set_xlabel("Day of week")
+ax.set_ylim(0, data["avg_crashes_per_day"].max() * 1.15)
+ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=20)
+ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_3.png", dpi=160)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+print(data[["weekday", "crash_count", "share_pct", "calendar_days", "avg_crashes_per_day"]].to_string(index=False))
+print(f"Total crashes: {total:,}")
*** End Patch

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/options.json
+{
+  "options": [
+    {
+      "id": 1,
+      "metric": "Number of police-reported crashes",
+      "denominator": "None; total crashes accumulated over the period",
+      "grouping": "Weekday (Monday through Sunday)",
+      "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+      "reason": "Raw totals give a direct view of how many reported crashes occurred on each weekday over the requested period.",
+      "probability": 0.38,
+      "answer": "Across 2013–2025, Friday had the most reported crashes (338,800) and Sunday the fewest (257,544)."
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 2,
+      "metric": "Share of all police-reported crashes",
+      "denominator": "All 2,132,218 crashes dated 2013–2025",
+      "grouping": "Weekday (Monday through Sunday)",
+      "chart_type": "Pie chart",
+      "reason": "Shares make each weekday's contribution to the full 13-year crash total easy to compare as parts of one whole.",
+      "probability": 0.32,
+      "answer": "Friday accounted for the largest share, 15.89% of crashes, while Sunday accounted for the smallest, 12.08%."
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 3,
+      "metric": "Average police-reported crashes per calendar occurrence of the weekday",
+      "denominator": "Calendar dates of that weekday from 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31 (678 or 679 dates, depending on weekday)",
+      "grouping": "Weekday (Monday through Sunday)",
+      "chart_type": "Line chart",
+      "reason": "Normalizing by the number of calendar occurrences accounts for the small differences in how often each weekday falls in the 13-year span.",
+      "probability": 0.30,
+      "answer": "The average was highest on Friday at 499.7 crashes per Friday and lowest on Sunday at 379.9 per Sunday."
+    }
+  ]
+}
*** Delete File: _make_weekday_outputs.py
*** End Patch
